target_customer: AI labs and robotics companies buying multimodal human data for robot training
problem: Robot learning is data starved. Human Archive records human movement with head mounted cameras, tactile gloves and sensors, largely from workers in India, to build large datasets.
business_model: Dataset sales (off the shelf and custom) plus robot deployments

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom sensor rigs and a large operations network across countries; the hard part is scale and data quality.

defensibility.rationale: Scale and low cost labor give an edge, but many 2026 entrants collect similar data and privacy concerns exist.

market_need_then: Labs buying egocentric video at scale; 2026 research showed gains from human video pretraining. Company claims 1,000+ headsets deployed and ability to collect up to 8,000 hours a day (self-reported).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven; has a Voice Rules page

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as the Common Crawl for embodied intelligence
branding.community_and_virality: Press from TechCrunch, Inc42, Gizmodo and Wing VC post in May 2026; some coverage raised worker privacy and pay concerns (about 1 dollar per hour base rate)

brand_strength.rationale: Clear analogy used by investors and press and wide coverage, though controversy over worker pay affects the brand.

outcome_analysis: Human Archive is an active W26 company that raised 8.2M in May 2026 from Wing, NVP and YC, and runs a large India based collection operation. Demand for egocentric data is strong but competitors are numerous and worker pay and privacy attract criticism. No outcome events found.
notes: Round reported by several outlets citing TechCrunch (2026-05-26); Pulse 2.0 does not name a lead while other reports say Wing led. Founding year not stated in sources opened. Contributor network claims vary (50,000+ on YC page, 100,000+ on RuntimeWire). Team size 100 includes a 25 person operations team per the YC page.
